[LSER.19.7] **First-assertion timestamp (`t_first`).** The runtime records,
per series instance (per `by:` identity), the timestamp of the first sample
absorbed into a fresh backing allocation — `t_first`. It is internal backing
state, not an author-facing value. An aggregation whose windowed estimate is biased low until a
full window of history exists may divide by the elapsed-aware denominator
`min(W, now − t_first)` instead of the full window `W`, removing the warm-up
undercount at no extra state or accuracy cost. `t_first` is set on the first
absorbed sample. Its consumer is `onset_rate`'s ÷`min(W, elapsed)` denominator,
whose state is never evicted ([LSER.9.3.1]), so `t_first` persists for the
instance's life and the correction applies over the instance's first `W` only.
